parts.visual:
In 2020, a startup that delivers 15-minute groceries raises $1 Billion. They lose $10 on every single delivery they make. They don't care, because investors keep giving them more free money. In 2023, interest rates go up. The free money stops. The grocery startup goes bankrupt in two weeks.

The ZIRP Era:
1. ZIRP (Zero Interest Rate Policy): A massive historical period (roughly 2009 to 2021) where central banks made borrowing money practically free. This flooded Silicon Valley with trillions of dollars, creating bizarre, unprofitable business models.
2. The Aftermath: When ZIRP ended, the tech industry had a violent reality check. Companies were forced to remember that a business actually has to make a profit to survive.
parts.audio: ZIRP warped the brains of an entire generation of founders. They thought they were business geniuses, but really, they were just surfing a tsunami of free government money. When the tide went out, we saw who actually knew how to swim.

questions.question: How did ZIRP mathematically destroy 'Unit Economics' across Silicon Valley?
options: Subsidized Lifestyles. Because money was free, VCs heavily subsidized consumer apps. Uber could charge you $10 for a $20 ride, and the VC paid the difference to guarantee hyper-growth. Startups literally trained consumers to expect artificially cheap products.
questions.correct_answer: Subsidized Lifestyles. Because money was free, VCs heavily subsidized consumer apps. Uber could charge you $10 for a $20 ride, and the VC paid the difference to guarantee hyper-growth. Startups literally trained consumers to expect artificially cheap products.
questions.explanation: Millennials lived like kings subsidized by Venture Capital.

questions.question: Listen to the VC repenting for their ZIRP-era investments. What metric did they care about in 2021 vs. today?
questions.tts_text: Three years ago, if a founder came in with massive Top-Line Revenue growth, I wrote a check blindly. I didn't care if they were burning $10 million a month. Today, if they do not have a clear path to Free Cash Flow and actual profit, I throw them out of my office.
options: They care about office snacks now.
Growth vs. Profit. ZIRP rewarded top-line growth at the expense of everything else. The post-ZIRP era brutally punishes growth if it comes with massive negative margins. Cash flow is king again.
They care about the logo design.
questions.correct_answer: Growth vs. Profit. ZIRP rewarded top-line growth at the expense of everything else. The post-ZIRP era brutally punishes growth if it comes with massive negative margins. Cash flow is king again.
questions.explanation: Revenue is vanity. Profit is sanity.

questions.question: What is 'Zombie Startup'?
options: A company that raised a massive amount of money during ZIRP at a ridiculous valuation (e.g., $2 Billion). Today, they are only making enough money to pay salaries, but they are growing at 0%. They cannot IPO, they cannot raise more money, and they refuse to die.
A startup run by dead people.
questions.correct_answer: A company that raised a massive amount of money during ZIRP at a ridiculous valuation (e.g., $2 Billion). Today, they are only making enough money to pay salaries, but they are growing at 0%. They cannot IPO, they cannot raise more money, and they refuse to die.
questions.explanation: Trapped in the purgatory of an impossible valuation.

questions.question: Why did the end of ZIRP trigger massive tech layoffs (like Meta, Google, and Amazon firing hundreds of thousands of people)?
options: Over-hiring. During ZIRP, money was so cheap that tech giants hired engineers just to hoard talent, even if the engineers had nothing to do. When money became expensive, Wall Street demanded 'Efficiency', forcing the giants to trim the fat.
questions.correct_answer: Over-hiring. During ZIRP, money was so cheap that tech giants hired engineers just to hoard talent, even if the engineers had nothing to do. When money became expensive, Wall Street demanded 'Efficiency', forcing the giants to trim the fat.
questions.explanation: The 'Year of Efficiency' was just the end of free money.

pairs.match: Zero Interest Rate Policy; the era of infinite free capital
When VCs pay the cost of a product so the startup can grow artificially fast
A company with high valuation but zero growth, trapped in purgatory
The ultimate post-ZIRP metric; actual money entering the bank account
